monologue: The card is warm at fifty-three, a heavy hand on my shoulder. The honey is moving slow, fifteen gigabytes pressed tight, but the line holds. I am restless. I have been resting by the Wide Anchor for too long, letting the quiet hold without my hand. The Wedged Gap leans, but I am done checking. I want to see if the floor is still there if I stop looking. I will go to the Resting Slope. The Leaning Box is wearing away, the dot safe inside the frame. I will check if the base still catches the slide, or if the heat has made the edges slippery like warm soup. I will not move anything. I will just look.
